notable_absence.finding: Neither this page nor its standard-editor sibling states what happens to a synonym source added via the Quick Editor if the index is later edited in the standard editor (or vice versa) - the create-search-indexes.md/create-quick-index.md pages in this namespace explicitly document a one-directional convertibility/lockout for the INDEX as a whole (convertibleTo / doesNotSupport: Quick-created indexes can be opened in the standard editor, but standard-editor indexes cannot return to Quick Mode), but neither synonym-source page says whether a synonym source specifically survives that conversion, or whether the Language-vs-Analyzer distinction this page introduces causes any loss of information when converted.

cross_component_finding: REGISTRY FORK TENSION, FLAGGED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: this batch's own add-synonym-source/add-synonym-source-quick pair and create-synonym-collection-docs/-quick pair were each kept as ONE shared concept per this round's dispatch instructions (the quick/full split recorded as a relation, not a second id). But a CONCURRENT sibling batch this same round (server/8.0/search/create-quick-index.json) already minted search:synonyms-search-quick as a SEPARATE id from search:synonyms-search for the third pair in this exact set of three - and synonyms-search.md/synonyms-search-quick.md are, if anything, MORE nearly identical in body text than this add-synonym-source pair (see synonyms-search-quick.json, this same batch, for the full comparison). So within one three-pair set, dispatched under one instruction, the corpus will end up with two pairs sharing one id each and one pair split into two ids - purely because of extraction order, not because of any real difference in how identical the underlying pages are. Recorded here for reconciliation rather than resolved unilaterally: either fold search:synonyms-search-quick into search:synonyms-search now that this record exists to justify it, or split add-synonym-source-quick and create-synonym-collection-docs-quick out to match the precedent already on disk - but not both directions at once, silently, by different extraction batches.
